subject.title: AgentConductor: Topology Evolution for Multi-Agent Competition-Level Code Generation

grade.component_causal_isolation: B- for SFT/RL/reward pieces; C for difficulty-partitioning and multi-turn-regeneration-specific effects

published_claims.headline: The abstract reports up to 14.6% pass@1 improvement, 13% density reduction and 68% token-cost reduction versus the strongest baseline.
published_claims.mechanism: A frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct orchestrator, trained by SFT then GRPO, emits difficulty-aware layered-DAG YAML topologies and can regenerate a later-turn topology from execution feedback/history, with at most two interaction turns.
published_claims.main_table: Table 2 reports mean±std over 3 runs; AgentConductor reports APPS 58.8±0.3, LiveCodeBench v4 46.3±0.4, CodeContests 38.8±0.5, HumanEval 97.5±0.1 and MBPP 95.1±0.2.

recomputation_and_scope_findings.finding: The abstract's 14.6% APPS headline is reproducible as a relative improvement, not as the absolute percentage-point margin stated later in Section 3.2.1.
recomputation_and_scope_findings.calculation: (58.8/51.3 - 1)*100 = 14.619883%; the absolute margin against the strongest APPS baseline MetaGPT 51.3 is 7.5 percentage points.
recomputation_and_scope_findings.scope: This is an internal reporting-unit inconsistency, not evidence that the underlying Table 2 values are false.

recomputation_and_scope_findings.finding: The 68% token-cost headline is not reconstructible from the displayed APPS Table 3 token counts under straightforward prompt-only, completion-only, or prompt+completion definitions.
recomputation_and_scope_findings.calculation: AgentConductor uses 277600 prompt + 79800 completion tokens. Across listed Table 3 baselines, the largest direct reductions are 47.77% prompt-only (vs AFlow), 60.12% completion-only (vs MacNet), and 50.10% total prompt+completion (vs AFlow).
recomputation_and_scope_findings.scope: A different denominator, aggregation, or cost definition may have been used, but it is not recoverable from the displayed table alone; therefore the 68% headline remains primary-study reporting rather than independently recomputed evidence.

recomputation_and_scope_findings.finding: The 13% density-reduction headline is not directly reproducible from Table 3's S_complex values as a raw density percentage.
recomputation_and_scope_findings.calculation: AgentConductor S_complex=5.2 while the largest listed baseline S_complex=4.1; the paper defines larger S_complex as sparser and the score is nonlinear. A direct percent-density interpretation is therefore not justified without the headline's exact aggregation/transform.
recomputation_and_scope_findings.scope: The qualitative claim that AgentConductor is sparsest in the displayed APPS table is supported; the exact 13% headline denominator remains under-specified.

component_evidence.evidence: Table 4 materially degrades without RL and loses most valid topology generation without SFT, supporting the importance of the training stages within the reported setup.
Table 4 separately removes YAML-error, code-error, node, edge, diameter and graph-density reward terms and reports performance/density/validity changes.
component_evidence.scope: Primary-study ablation only; interactions among terms remain possible.

component_evidence.evidence: The paper reports per-difficulty density behavior and fixed per-turn node caps 4/7/10, but the audited ablation table does not contain a matched fixed-density/no-difficulty-partition arm.
component_evidence.scope: The specific causal contribution of difficulty interval partitioning is not isolated.

component_evidence.evidence: The algorithm and implementation description clearly specify regeneration from execution feedback/history up to K=2, but the audited ablation table does not compare matched static/one-turn versus regenerated/two-turn topologies.
component_evidence.scope: The specific causal contribution of online topology regeneration is not isolated.

supported: Detailed algorithm/pseudocode and topology semantics are published.
SFT sample construction is described, including 4500 total examples.

Major training settings are given: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, LLaMA-Factory SFT LR 1e-4 batch 4 LoRA; Verl/vLLM GRPO group 8 batch 8 LR 1e-6 temperature 1 max completion 4096; maximum turns 2; worker gpt-4o-mini; 4xA800.
blockers: No author-affiliated public runtime repository, exact trained orchestrator checkpoint, raw benchmark run bundle, or exact SFT/RL dataset artifact was located in this audit's public search.
The paper states that all other SFT hyperparameters use framework defaults, making exact replay version-sensitive unless exact LLaMA-Factory/PEFT/tokenizer/runtime versions are pinned.
Random seeds for the main code-generation runs are not exposed in the audited text despite Table 2 reporting three-run statistics.
The precise denominator/aggregation for the 68% token and 13% density headlines is not recoverable from the displayed table values alone.

independent_artifact.status: Independent approximate reimplementation, not an author artifact and not a matched numerical replication.
positive_evidence: README explicitly identifies arXiv:2602.17100v1 as the target and labels its own claim 'approximate reproduction'.

The repository implements typed topology contracts, deterministic and learned orchestrator boundaries, multi-turn solve state/revision, checkpoint-backed local inference, graph execution, APPS-style ingestion, local multi-language benchmark paths and grouped RL-style update artifacts.
The project has source and tests, making several mechanism-level interfaces inspectable.
limitations: README explicitly says the full paper runtime and exact paper-scale checkpoint/leaderboard reproduction are not implemented.
Default model-facing execution includes repository-local substitutes/stubs rather than the paper's live gpt-4o-mini/benchmark serving path.
pyproject dependencies are lower-bounded rather than exact-pinned and the audited top-level listing did not expose an environment lock file.
README refers to docs/reproduction.md, but the audited docs directory contains only tasks.md; this is a minor documentation/replay-path inconsistency, not evidence against the paper mechanism.

independent_replication_search.note: A substantial independent approximate implementation was found, but no public result located in this audit reproduced the paper's five benchmark headline table under the same trained orchestrator, worker model, data, budgets and sandbox.

safe_interpretation: AgentConductor has detailed primary-study evidence and enough specification for meaningful mechanism reimplementation. The strongest supported external claim is that the dynamic layered-DAG orchestration design is concretely implementable; the exact benchmark gains and cost/density headlines remain primary-study results because an author execution artifact and protocol-matched independent rerun were not located. The SFT/RL/reward ablations should not be generalized into evidence that difficulty partitioning or multi-turn regeneration individually causes the full gain.
reopen_conditions: Author-affiliated code/checkpoint/data/raw benchmark bundle becomes public.
A protocol-matched independent rerun reproduces or fails to reproduce the Table 2/3 results.
The authors publish the exact 68% token-cost and 13% density reduction aggregation/denominator.
A matched ablation isolates difficulty-aware partitioning or within-instance topology regeneration.
exact_next_action: Do not re-audit unchanged AgentConductor. On the next bootstrap-valid invocation, freeze the then-exact wave and audit a different source-qualified non-evaluation candidate with executable official material; prefer TraceElephant, AgentRewind, a new open_source candidate, or a source-matched cross_field mechanism.
